title: Quarterly Slicing & Prioritization: Hosted API + Model Catalog Decision Rail
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a lightweight, repeatable quarterly decision rail for slicing the Hosted API product surface and prioritizing model-catalog work. This ticket captures the decision criteria, slice definitions, and operational rules we will use to: 1) pick which models/endpoints enter the next quarter's commit window, 2) allocate engineering cadence (canary vs steady rollout), and 3) set OKR-linked acceptance thresholds.

Scope: Hosted API endpoints and associated model variants in the central model catalog. Includes: curated model onboarding, retirement candidates, canary scheduling, quality guardrails (eval sets), and cost/latency constraint bins. Excludes: Dedicated and Private deployment-specific infra changes (handled by separate initiative).

Why now: Quarterly planning has drifted toward ad-hoc decisions. This decision rail reduces stakeholder friction, clarifies trade-offs between latency/cost/quality, and provides a deterministic tie to OKR targets for model availability and unit-cost improvements.

Key outputs from this ticket: a) "Slice" taxonomy (User-facing priority slices, Cost-sensitivity buckets, Latency-critical lanes), b) Prioritization rubric with weighted criteria (customer reach, OKR delta, infra cost delta, regression risk), c) Canary and rollout rules per slice (canary size, duration, health metrics), d) A short-run channel list of model candidates mapped to slices for the upcoming quarter, e) Evaluation checklist and required artifacts for acceptance (prompts, eval dashboards, PRs), f) Owner matrix and dependencies for execution.
acceptance_criteria: Published one-page decision rail doc in Confluence with slice definitions and weighted rubric
Prioritized list of model + endpoint candidates (top 12) mapped to slices for Q2 planning
Clear rollout rules (canary %, SLOs monitored, fallback plan) for each slice type
OKR mapping: each prioritized candidate shows expected impact on at least one existing OKR metric
Cross-functional sign-off from Eng Reliability, Applied ML (model health), and DevExp by the due date
metrics_and_success_criteria: Time-to-decision for model onboarding reduced from current median 12 days to <=5 days
At least 80% of prioritized candidates have automated eval sets and perf baselines before rollout
Fewer than 2 production regressions attributable to model swaps in the quarter after applying the decision rail
Ability to explain cost delta and latency impact for each candidate within 1 hour during planning review
notes_and_decisions: 2025-03-03: Initial slice taxonomy approved in sync — three primary slices: 'Core PLG', 'Enterprise SLA', 'Cost Hedge'.
Decision: Use weighted rubric where quality/regression risk has 35% weight, customer reach 30%, cost delta 20%, infra effort 15%.
Sunset rule: any model candidate with unresolved critical eval regressions after two canary cycles will be moved to 'defer' and re-evaluated in the next quarter.
Canary rule: For 'Enterprise SLA' lane, minimum canary coverage 5% traffic for at least 72 hours with no P1 latency or accuracy regressions before rolling to 50%.
